header.title: Curse tablets from Raetia (Epigraphic Database Heidelberg): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Latin curse tablets
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:defix:edh:raetia:lat, from the Epigraphic Database Heidelberg (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.17875.2.7: Fragments of three tablets. 17875: '[ipi]atis' completes the 'cor-' that ends the preceding line, cor[ipi]atis, 'that you (plural) seize'; the next line is lost. 19906: Muta Tacita is the goddess of silence; each later 'Mutae' could be the goddess ('to Muta') rather than plural 'Mute Ones', and the repeated formula is obscure; 'rutus' is doubtful (perhaps for ruptus, 'broken'); the 'golden gates' are unexplained. 57898: AMC is unexplained, perhaps initials; 'ad era(m)' is unclear ('to the Lady', or perhaps 'to the altar'); Ogmius is the Celtic god Ogmios. The edition gives some words in several spellings separated by # (normalised, and as written: IMPLEID, CUR, TALUS); each word is translated once, so 'will fulfil' (implebit) runs over the tablet's first three lines.
notes.58312.1.5: 'against' completes 'adve-' at the end of the preceding line (adve-rsus). Ogmius is the Celtic god Ogmios. In line 2.3 letters before and after DM are erased on the tablet; DM...O and DIM...O are unexplained. Niger and Valerius (accusative, so among those cursed) are names; the surrounding words are lost.

nodes.text: [... that you] se[i]ze [...]
To Muta Tacita: that he may be mute,
Quartus; harried, may he wander like a mouse
in flight, or a bird facing a basilisk,
that h[i]s mouth may be mute. Mute Ones!
Mute Ones, may they be [d]ire! Mute Ones,
may they be silent! Mute Ones,
that [Qu]a[rt]us may go mad.
That he may be cast down (?) to the Erinyes, and
Quartus to Orcus; that the Mute Ones,
silent — that they may [be] mute
at the golden gates.
I bind AMC, that thing. [He] will ful-
-fil [it]:
Dis Pater, to the Lady (?), Ogmius:
health, heart, ankles, ki[dneys]
against her speaks — all of them
may you de[str]oy.
[I a]sk you all, [w]ho for her
are [pre]paring evil to be given:
[...]DM[...]O to be given to O[g]mius, to be [con]-
sumed by deat[h] [...]T[...]T[...]NTI and Nige[r] [...]
DIM[...]O Valerius
